subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should WhatsApp auth become a dedicated plugin-owned SQLite store, and what migration, rollback, backup-retention, and credential-protection contract must it satisfy?
rationale: This changes the canonical persistence and security boundary for shipped authentication credentials and cryptographic session state, so automation should not choose the schema or irreversible migration policy.

options.title: Dedicated plugin SQLite store
options.body: Use a WhatsApp-owned relational schema with transactional migration, verification, recovery, and explicit legacy-file cleanup semantics.

options.title: Shared plugin keyed state
options.body: Use the generic plugin keyed-state API only after proving its JSON, size, eviction, and transaction constraints fit every Baileys key category.

options.title: Retain hardened files
options.body: Keep the multi-file format and continue targeted atomicity, recovery, and load-performance hardening without changing the canonical store.

recommendation.title: Dedicated plugin SQLite store
recommendation.body: Use a WhatsApp-owned relational schema with transactional migration, verification, recovery, and explicit legacy-file cleanup semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history signal spans the WhatsApp session/auth-store boundary, and this person has already provided maintainer-side review context on the issue.
